# Material usage types
{: .no_toc}

Detail schemas for material usage rows: one material in one role, as prepared or applied in a procedure, specimen procedure or experimental interface. The role (type) selects the schema.

## Devices

Implanted, inserted or attached devices for recording, stimulation, imaging, sensing or fluid delivery, recorded with their sterility and use-specific preparation.

### Blood-pressure sensor

A blood-pressure sensor or telemetry transmitter implanted or attached to measure arterial or venous pressure, with its sterility and any surface treatment.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Sterility status` | Choice. Sterility status of this material when it was used. Options: Sterile, Not sterile, Unknown. |
| `Sterilization method` | Choice. Method used to sterilize this material. Options: Autoclave, Ethylene oxide, Gamma irradiation, Other, None, Unknown. |
| `Disinfection method` | Choice. Method used to disinfect this material. Options: Alcohol, Chlorhexidine, Povidone-iodine, Other, None, Unknown. |
| `Surface treatment or coating` | Text. Use-specific surface treatment or coating applied to this device or component. |

| `Flush volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume used to flush the line for this use. Units: mL, µL, nL. |
| `End preparation` | Text. Preparation of the delivery end before use. |
| `Sterility status` | Choice. Sterility status of the line when used. Options: Sterile, Not sterile, Unknown. |

## Components and supporting materials

Hardware and materials that hold, position, protect or fix an implant or specimen, such as cements, fasteners, microdrives, headcaps and slides.

### Adhesive, cement, or sealant

A glue, dental or bone cement, or sealant used to secure an implant or seal tissue, with the amount used, mixing ratio, application method and area, and curing method, duration and temperature.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Applied volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume of this material used in this record. When the parent records a total volume, this is this material's share of that total. Units: L, mL, µL, nL. |
| `Applied mass` | Quantity with unit. Mass of this material used in this record. Units: kg, g, mg, µg, ng. |
| `Mixing ratio` | Ratio. Component ratio used to prepare a multi-part material. |
| `Mixing ratio › numerator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |
| `Mixing ratio › denominator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |
| `Application method` | Text. How this material was applied in this usage. |
| `Applied area` | Text. Location or surface where this material was applied. |
| `Curing method` | Choice. Curing, drying, rinsing, or other post-application treatment. Options: Self-cured, Air dried, Heat cured, UV cured, Chemical cure, None, Other. |
| `Curing duration` | Quantity with unit. Duration allowed for curing, drying, or another post-treatment. Units: d, h, min, s. |
| `Curing temperature` | Quantity with unit. Temperature used during curing or another post-treatment. Units: °C, K. |

### Baseplate

A baseplate fixed to the skull or headcap to which a removable device, such as a head-mounted miniature microscope, is attached.

This type has no type-specific fields. The record's own fields and its material rows describe it.

### Coating

A coating applied to a device or component before use, such as a lipophilic dye on a probe shank, with the coated area, application method, concentration and number of coats.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Application method` | Text. How this material was applied in this usage. |
| `Coated area` | Text. Part of the device or component that was coated. |
| `Applied concentration` | Quantity with unit. Concentration of this material in the formulation or mixture actually applied. Units: M, mM, µM, nM, g/L, mg/mL, µg/mL, ng/mL, mg/L, µg/L, ng/L, % w/v, % v/v. |
| `Number of coats` | Integer. Number of coating layers applied. Range: ≥ 1. |

| Field | Description |

| `Preparation` | Text. Use-specific preparation of this material, such as mixing, dilution, trimming, or another treatment. |

### Fixed implant carrier or shuttle

A fixed carrier or shuttle that holds a device at a set position without a movable drive, with how the device is attached, how the carrier is fixed, whether the device can be recovered, and sterility.

| Field | Description |

## Agents and drugs

Pharmacologically active substances given to a subject or applied to tissue, recorded with the amount of each agent itself rather than of the mixture it was part of.

### Active agent

The pharmacologically active substance of a formulation given or applied in a procedure, when no more specific drug role fits, with this agent's own dose, concentration, dilution, volume or mass.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Applied dose` | Quantity with unit. This agent's own dose in this record, normalized to body mass; never the mixture's combined dose. Units: g/kg, mg/kg, µg/kg, ng/kg. |
| `Applied concentration` | Quantity with unit. This agent's own strength in the formulation as prepared, not the formulation's overall strength. Units: M, mM, µM, nM, g/L, mg/mL, µg/mL, ng/mL, mg/L, µg/L, ng/L, % w/v, % v/v. |
| `Applied dilution` | Ratio. Ratio by which this agent's own source material was diluted to prepare it for this use. |
| `Applied dilution › numerator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |
| `Applied dilution › denominator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |
| `Applied volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume this agent itself contributed here — its own share of any total the parent records. Units: L, mL, µL, nL. |
| `Applied mass` | Quantity with unit. Absolute amount of this agent contributed here: weighed or fixed, not calculated per body mass. Units: kg, g, mg, µg, ng. |
| `Preparation` | Text. Prose about preparing this agent here. Row order already records addition order, and a recipe that must be followed belongs in a linked protocol. |

### Anesthetic agent

An anesthetic drug given for induction or maintenance, with this agent's own dose, concentration and volume, also when it is one component of a cocktail. A vaporizer setting for an inhaled agent belongs on the event, not here.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Applied dose` | Quantity with unit. This agent's own dose in this anesthetic, normalized to body mass; never the cocktail's total. Units: g/kg, mg/kg, µg/kg, ng/kg. |
| `Applied concentration` | Quantity with unit. This agent's own strength in the solution as drawn up; a vaporizer setting belongs on the event. Units: M, mM, µM, nM, g/L, mg/mL, µg/mL, ng/mL, mg/L, µg/L, ng/L, % w/v, % v/v. |
| `Applied volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume this agent itself contributed to the mixture; an inhaled agent has no volume here. Units: L, mL, µL, nL. |

### Anticoagulant

An anticoagulant such as heparin used to keep blood, catheters or delivery lines from clotting, with the applied concentration, dilution and volume.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Applied concentration` | Quantity with unit. Concentration of this material in the formulation or mixture actually applied. Units: M, mM, µM, nM, g/L, mg/mL, µg/mL, ng/mL, mg/L, µg/L, ng/L, % w/v, % v/v. |
| `Applied dilution` | Ratio. Dilution of the source material used to prepare the applied formulation, expressed as a ratio. |
| `Applied dilution › numerator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |
| `Applied dilution › denominator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |
| `Applied volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume of this material used in this record. When the parent records a total volume, this is this material's share of that total. Units: L, mL, µL, nL. |
| `Preparation` | Text. Use-specific preparation of this material, such as mixing, dilution, trimming, or another treatment. |

A material or agent applied to control bleeding, such as a gelatin sponge, bone wax or topical hemostat, with the amount or number of pieces used and how it was applied.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Applied volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume of this material used in this record. When the parent records a total volume, this is this material's share of that total. Units: L, mL, µL, nL. |
| `Applied mass` | Quantity with unit. Mass of this material used in this record. Units: kg, g, mg, µg, ng. |
| `Count used` | Integer. Number of items of this material used in this record. Range: ≥ 1. |
| `Preparation` | Text. Use-specific preparation of this material, such as mixing, dilution, trimming, or another treatment. |
| `Application method` | Text. How this material was applied in this usage. |

A gas or inhalant used for euthanasia, such as CO2 or an overdose of isoflurane, with the applied concentration, flow rate and duration of exposure.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|

| `Applied flow rate` | Quantity with unit. Flow rate at which this gas was applied or delivered. Units: L/min, mL/min, µL/min, nL/min. |
| `Application duration` | Quantity with unit. Duration for which this material was actively applied or delivered. Units: d, h, min, s. |

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|

| `Applied concentration` | Quantity with unit. Concentration of this material in the formulation or mixture actually applied. Units: M, mM, µM, nM, g/L, mg/mL, µg/mL, ng/mL, mg/L, µg/L, ng/L, % w/v, % v/v. |
| `Applied dilution` | Ratio. Dilution of the source material used to prepare the applied formulation, expressed as a ratio. |
| `Applied dilution › numerator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |
| `Applied dilution › denominator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |
| `Applied volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume of this material used in this record. When the parent records a total volume, this is this material's share of that total. Units: L, mL, µL, nL. |
| `Applied mass` | Quantity with unit. Mass of this material used in this record. Units: kg, g, mg, µg, ng. |
| `Preparation` | Text. Use-specific preparation of this material, such as mixing, dilution, trimming, or another treatment. |

A substance used to produce a chemical or excitotoxic lesion, such as ibotenic acid or 6-OHDA, with the applied dose, concentration, volume and application method.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Applied dose` | Quantity with unit. Dose of this material administered or applied in this usage. Units: g/kg, mg/kg, µg/kg, ng/kg. |
| `Applied concentration` | Quantity with unit. Concentration of this material in the formulation or mixture actually applied. Units: M, mM, µM, nM, g/L, mg/mL, µg/mL, ng/mL, mg/L, µg/L, ng/L, % w/v, % v/v. |
| `Applied dilution` | Ratio. Dilution of the source material used to prepare the applied formulation, expressed as a ratio. |

| `Applied dilution › denominator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |

| `Applied mass` | Quantity with unit. Mass of this material used in this record. Units: kg, g, mg, µg, ng. |
| `Preparation` | Text. Use-specific preparation of this material, such as mixing, dilution, trimming, or another treatment. |
| `Application method` | Text. How this material was applied in this usage. |

### Pharmacological adjunct

A substance added alongside the main agent to modify its effect or delivery, such as a vasoconstrictor or an enzyme, with its own dose, concentration or activity units per volume and the reason it was added.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Applied dose` | Quantity with unit. Dose of this substance itself, per unit body mass, not of the mixture it was part of. Units: g/kg, mg/kg, µg/kg, ng/kg. |
| `Applied concentration` | Quantity with unit. Concentration this substance reached in the mixture as applied, after any dilution. Units: M, mM, µM, nM, g/L, mg/mL, µg/mL, ng/mL, mg/L, µg/L, ng/L, % w/v, % v/v. |
| `Applied dilution` | Ratio. How far the source material was diluted to prepare what was applied here. |

| `Applied dilution › denominator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |
| `Applied volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume of this substance itself that was added, not of the whole mixture. Units: L, mL, µL, nL. |
| `Applied mass` | Quantity with unit. Mass of this substance itself that was added, not of the whole mixture. Units: kg, g, mg, µg, ng. |
| `Applied activity concentration` | Quantity with unit. Biological activity units of this substance per volume of the mixture as applied, not an infectious titer. Units: IU/mL, U/mL, USP units/mL. |
| `Purpose` | Choice. Why this substance was added alongside the main agent. Options: Vasoconstriction, pH buffering, Block prolongation, Tissue spread, Irritation reduction, Autonomic counteraction, Sedation deepening, Other. |

### Reversal agent

A drug given to reverse an anesthetic or sedative, such as atipamezole after medetomidine, with the applied dose, concentration and volume, the dose it was chosen against, and whether reversal was meant to be full or partial.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Applied dose` | Quantity with unit. Dose of this substance itself, per unit body mass, not of the mixture it was part of. Units: g/kg, mg/kg, µg/kg, ng/kg. |
| `Applied concentration` | Quantity with unit. Concentration this substance reached in the mixture as applied, after any dilution. Units: M, mM, µM, nM, g/L, mg/mL, µg/mL, ng/mL, mg/L, µg/L, ng/L, % w/v, % v/v. |
| `Applied volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume of this substance itself that was administered, not of the whole mixture. Units: L, mL, µL, nL. |
| `Relative dose basis` | Choice. What this reversal dose was chosen against. Options: Agonist's dose, Agonist's volume, Fixed amount per animal, Titrated to effect, Other. |
| `Purpose` | Choice. Whether reversal was intended to be full or deliberately partial. Options: Full reversal, Partial reversal, Other. |

### Supportive-care agent

A drug given for supportive or perioperative care, such as an analgesic, anti-inflammatory, antibiotic or ophthalmic ointment, with the applied dose, concentration, dilution, volume or mass.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|

| `Applied dilution › denominator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |
| `Applied volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume of this material used in this record. When the parent records a total volume, this is this material's share of that total. Units: L, mL, µL, nL. |
| `Applied mass` | Quantity with unit. Mass of this material used in this record. Units: kg, g, mg, µg, ng. |
| `Preparation` | Text. Use-specific preparation of this material, such as mixing, dilution, trimming, or another treatment. |

## Biological and experimental payloads

Viral vectors, cells, tracers, particles and other components delivered into tissue, recorded with the titer, count, concentration or volume actually delivered.

### Cell suspension

A suspension of cells delivered into tissue, for example for transplantation, with the applied cell count and concentration, viability before application, volume and passage number of cultured cells.

| `Cell viability` | Number. Measured viable-cell percentage immediately before application. Range: ≥ 0 and ≤ 100. |
| `Applied volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume of cell suspension applied. Units: mL, µL, nL. |
| `Passage number at use` | Integer. Passage number of cultured cells at the time the suspension was prepared. Range: ≥ 0. |
| `Preparation` | Text. Use-specific preparation of the cell suspension. |

### Injected component

One component of an injected or infused formulation when no more specific payload role fits, with its applied dose, concentration, volume, mass or count and its fraction of the final formulation.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|

| `Applied concentration` | Quantity with unit. Concentration of this material in the formulation or mixture actually applied. Units: M, mM, µM, nM, g/L, mg/mL, µg/mL, ng/mL, mg/L, µg/L, ng/L, % w/v, % v/v. |
| `Applied dilution` | Ratio. Dilution of the source material used to prepare the applied formulation, expressed as a ratio. |
| `Applied dilution › numerator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |
| `Applied dilution › denominator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |
| `Applied volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume of this material used in this record. When the parent records a total volume, this is this material's share of that total. Units: L, mL, µL, nL. |
| `Applied mass` | Quantity with unit. Mass of this material used in this record. Units: kg, g, mg, µg, ng. |
| `Count used` | Integer. Number of items of this material used in this record. Range: ≥ 1. |
| `Fraction of applied formulation` | Number. Fraction of the final applied formulation contributed by this component, entered from 0 to 1 (for example, 0.5 for 50%). Range: ≥ 0 and ≤ 1. |
| `Preparation` | Text. Use-specific preparation of this material, such as mixing, dilution, trimming, or another treatment. |

## Fluids and vehicles

Fluids, carrier gases and vehicles that are administered or that carry an active agent, and additives mixed into such fluids.

### Administered fluid

A fluid given to a subject, such as saline or lactated Ringer's for fluid support, with the volume of this fluid given.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Applied volume` | Quantity with unit. How much of this fluid was given, as its own share. It is not the event's combined total, even when this is the only fluid and the numbers match. Units: L, mL, µL. |

### Carrier gas

The gas that carries an inhaled anesthetic or is supplied for breathing, such as oxygen or medical air, with the applied flow rate and concentration.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Applied flow rate` | Quantity with unit. Flow rate at which this gas was applied or delivered. Units: L/min, mL/min, µL/min, nL/min. |
| `Applied concentration` | Quantity with unit. Concentration of this material in the formulation or mixture actually applied. Units: % v/v, ppm. |

### Fluid additive

A substance added to a fluid, such as drinking water or a perfusion reservoir, with the concentration reached after mixing, the amount added, and whether an equal volume was withdrawn first.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Applied concentration` | Quantity with unit. Concentration this additive reached in the fluid that was delivered, after mixing. Not the strength of the concentrate or stock it was drawn from. Units: M, mM, µM, nM, g/L, mg/mL, µg/mL, ng/mL, mg/L, µg/L, ng/L, % w/v, % v/v. |
| `Applied volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume of this additive alone that was put into the fluid. Not the volume of the fluid it went into. Units: L, mL, µL. |
| `Applied mass` | Quantity with unit. Mass of this additive alone that was put into the fluid, when mass rather than volume was the quantity actually measured. Units: kg, g, mg, µg, ng. |
| `Replacement method` | Choice. Whether an equal volume was withdrawn before this additive went in, which decides whether the stated concentration was actually reached. Options: Equal volume withdrawn first, Added to a full container, Not recorded. |

### Irrigation solution

A solution used to rinse or keep tissue moist during a procedure, such as sterile saline or aCSF, with the applied concentration, dilution and volume.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|

| `Applied dilution › numerator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |
| `Applied dilution › denominator` | **Required.** Number. Range: > 0. |
| `Applied volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume of this material used in this record. When the parent records a total volume, this is this material's share of that total. Units: L, mL, µL, nL. |
| `Preparation` | Text. Use-specific preparation of this material, such as mixing, dilution, trimming, or another treatment. |

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
